Subject: ISO 27001 scope + FedRAMP readiness — clarifications and evidence asks

Hi team,

Following up from Friday's compliance sync — Beacon Health has asked for a compact timeline and a clear scoping decision for ISO 27001 and the FedRAMP Moderate assessment request they raised. Jane (copied) is helping them run through required artifacts and will help map overlap with our SOC 2 / SIG evidence.

I need three clarifications so we can reply to Beacon by EOD Wednesday:

1) Target ISO 27001 scope — do we include Redwood Private (VPC) + Dedicated pools by default, or limit the initial scope to the Hosted API only? Pros/cons we should call out (e.g., on-prem variance for evidence).

2) FedRAMP scoping baseline — Beacon is asking whether the Moderate baseline will require HSM/KMS attestations and if our current KMS controls (see attached design) are sufficient. If anyone from infra/security can confirm whether HSM-backed keys are in production for Dedicated/Private, flag now.

3) Evidence sampling window and upcoming audits — Beacon expects evidence covering a 6-month window for their internal review and is planning an auditor check in late June. We need to map control owners and who can provide:
   - Access logs and retention proof (IAM & infra)
   - Change management tickets for runtime components (serving runtime)
   - Network diagrams and VPC peering configs for Private deployments

Attachments: redwood_control_matrix_v2.xlsx (latest control mapping).

Action items:
- Marissa: can you confirm ISO scope recommendation and any blockers for including Private?
- Vivek: confirm KMS/HSM production state for Dedicated and Private and whether we can produce HSM attestation or only KMS key rotation logs.
- Karthik: helper on auditor timeline? if late June is tight, propose alternate windows.

Jane — if you can outline the minimum artifacts Beacon will require for a FedRAMP Moderate pre-check, that helps us prioritize.

Thanks,

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Compliance Programs (interim)
Redwood Inference

Thanks Steph — quick notes from product/compliance side: 

- My recommendation: start ISO 27001 scope with Hosted API and Dedicated pools only. Private (VPC/on-prem) brings a lot of customer-specific network/config artifacts that blow up evidence volume and timelines. We can stage Private in a later annex (v1 scope = hosted + dedicated).

- On the FedRAMP side, Beacon will likely expect KMS attestation for keys used to protect moderate-impact data. We currently use cloud KMS with customer-managed keys for Dedicated, and an HSM-backed KMS option is being piloted in Private but not fully rolled out. I can extract a short matrix showing which environments have HSM-backed keys by EOD Tuesday.

- For evidence owners: I'll volunteer to own Network diagrams + VPC peering docs for Dedicated + Hosted, but we'll need infra to pull the actual diagrams and peering configs.

Minor ask: can we avoid sending full ticket exports to Beacon until we redact internal-only identifiers? We can provide aggregated change management exports.

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Compliance Program Manager

Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ISO 27001 scope + FedRAMP readiness — clarifications and evidence asks

Hi all — thanks for the context. Short answers and checklist below. I attached a gap-assessment-template.xlsx you can use to mark availability per artifact.

1) ISO scope: starting with Hosted + Dedicated is pragmatic. Auditor will accept staged scope as long as scope decision is documented and communicated to stakeholders; we usually capture Private in a follow-up annex.

2) FedRAMP Moderate: HSM-backed key attestations are common but not strictly required if compensating controls are documented and keys are logically isolated with appropriate access controls and audit logs. What matters for FedRAMP assessors is demonstrable key management lifecycle (provisioning, rotation, destruction) + separation of duties. If you have KMS rotation logs, IAM roles for key management, and an architecture diagram, we can build the narrative. If you have any HSM attestation/cert doc, include it — that'll shorten the assessor's queries.

3) Evidence sampling windows: for a pre-audit review, Beacon's internal team will be satisfied with a rolling 6-month window ending the month before the auditor visit. So for a late-June auditor check, provide Jan–May artifacts. For SOC 2 overlap: most infra controls (change mgmt, logging, patching) map directly — use the control matrix to mark overlaps so we avoid duplicate exports.

Immediate asks:
- Provide the KMS rotation log extract (Jan–May) and any HSM attestation PDF if available.
- Network diagrams (high-level) and a short narrative describing VPC isolation for Dedicated and Hosted.
- Redacted change management exports for the serving runtime (ticket ids redacted) covering Jan–May.

If you'd like, we can run a 90-minute gap session on Wed (14 Apr) to triage artifacts; I can host and bring a checklist that lines up FedRAMP vs ISO vs SOC2/CAIQ.

Regards,

Jane Doe
Principal Consultant — Regulatory Consult LLC
jane.doe@regulatoryconsult.com

Thanks — quick status and next steps (TL;DR below).

Status:
- KMS/HSM: Dedicated and Hosted use cloud KMS with customer-managed keys; we do not yet have a production HSM attestation. Private has an HSM-backed option in pilot (pilot region eu-west-1) but not in prod. I've attached a short design diagram (kms-hsm-design-diagram.pdf) to show current boundaries.

- Logs & Tickets: SRE can produce rotation logs and IAM audit logs for Jan–May. Change management exports for the serving runtime require redaction; I will coordinate with SRE to produce redacted exports by next Tuesday (20 Apr).

- Network diagrams: Marissa will own high-level diagrams; infra will supply exported peering configs to be redacted as needed.

Action / Timeline: 
1) Wed 14 Apr — run the 90-minute gap session (Jane to lead). I'll schedule for 10:00 PT; invite sent.
2) Tue 20 Apr — provide KMS rotation logs (Jan–May) and redacted change mgmt exports.
3) Fri 23 Apr — deliver high-level network diagrams (Marissa + infra).
4) Wed 28 Apr — internal review of artifacts and final prep for Beacon's pre-check.

Owners:
- KMS logs & design: Vivek (infra/SRE)
- Network diagrams & scope doc: Marissa
- Auditor scheduling and timeline: Karthik

If Beacon still prefers Private in initial ISO scope, we can re-evaluate but recommend keeping Private out for v1 to reduce evidence volume.

Thanks everyone — I'll follow up with invites and a small task list in the shared Drive folder.

--
